title: Ohm's law, Kirchhoff's laws, dividers and the Wheatstone bridge
goal: Predict and measure currents and voltages in series and parallel networks, confirm KVL and KCL, and balance a Wheatstone bridge.
theory: Ohm's law: V = I·R. Around any closed loop the voltage rises equal the drops (KVL); at any node the currents in equal the currents out (KCL).

In a series string the same current flows through every resistor, so each takes a share of the supply proportional to its resistance (voltage divider). Parallel branches share the same voltage and split the current in inverse proportion to their resistance (current divider).

A Wheatstone bridge is two dividers side by side. When R1/R2 = R3/Rx their midpoints sit at the same voltage and a meter between them reads zero — a null measurement that does not depend on the supply voltage.

prelab.label: Series current with 1 kΩ, 2.2 kΩ, 3.3 kΩ on 10 V
Node voltage: 1 kΩ feeding 2 kΩ ∥ 3 kΩ
Rx that balances the bridge (R7 = R8 = R9 = 1 kΩ)

procedure: Load the reference build: a series string (R1–R3), a parallel network (R6 feeding R4 ∥ R5) and a bridge (R7–R9 and the decade box RX).
Measure the voltage across each series resistor with M1 and check that they add up to the supply (KVL).
Measure the node voltage of the parallel network; compute the current in R4 and R5 and check they add to the current in R6 (KCL).
Put M1 between the two bridge midpoints (c33 and c38) and adjust RX until it reads zero.

checks.label: Series string: R3 takes its share (KVL)
